text.p: The following are the main stories from Wednesday morning's German newspapers:
FRANKFURTER ALLGEMEINE ZEITUNG
- Thousands of miners continue protests in Bonn as talks on coal subsidies are postponed
- Health Minister Horst Seehofer and CDU agree on higher patient contributions in health reform
- Failure of tax talks grows more likely
- Exports to rise five percent in 1997, association says.
- Parliament to correct errors made by East Germany in nationalising property
- Economic research institute HWWA says Germany will fail to meet criteria for single currency
HANDELSBLATT
- Chancellor Kohl refuses to hold talks with miners' union while street protests continue
- Price-setting agreements for text CD-ROMs are legal, court rules
- Hoechst results disappoint market, Bayer in line with expectations
- Compromise in sight in row between VW and EU on subsidies for east German plant
- Deutsche Telekom confirms profits to be more than doubled this year
- Exports to drive growth in 1997, association says
- Volksbanken savings banks say delay in single currency now possible
- Price slump in consumer electronics continues
- Thomson makes final decision to end television production in Germany
SUEDDEUTSCHE ZEITUNG
- Coal miners storm Bonn government exclusion zone
- Cabinet agrees higher sentences for sex crimes
- Exports continue to drive German growth
- Bankruptcies rise more strongly in Germany than elsewhere in Europe
- Road, rail and air traffic to resume growth in 1997, Ifo institute says
- HWWA institute sees hardly any fall in unemployment in 1998
- Deutsche Telekom says it is ready for open competition, confirms expected profit rise
DIE WELT
- Chancellor Kohl postpones coal talks as protests escalate
- Coalition approves new plan for health insurance reform
- Ombudswoman bemoans poor level of equipment in German army
- Deutsche Telekom to double profits in 1997
- No new date set for tax talks between government and opposition Social Democrats
- Economics Minister Rexrodt says subsidies for east German economy to be kept at high level
- Exports continue to drive growth
- Engineering union IG Metall to fight for more part-time work for older employees
